newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TASMANIA MOVE CLOSER TO SHIELD FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TASMANIA MOVE CLOSER TO SHIELD FINAL.

text.p: Tasmania strengthened their chance of making the Sheffield Shield final when they moved to 207 for four at stumps on the third day of their four-day match against Queensland at the Bellerive Oval in Hobart on Sunday.
Tasmania, who have never won Australia's domestic first-class competition, took an overall lead of 332 after dismissing Queensland for 283 earlier in the day.

The Tasmanians had set the pace in the game with a first innings of 408 and opener Jamie Cox gave his side the perfect foundation in their second innings with a brisk 74 while Michael DiVenuto weighed in with 56.

Tasmania are second in the Shield standings on 24 points, 12 behind leaders Western Australia who booked their place in the final later this month when they beat New South Wales by nine wickets on the second day of their match on Saturday.
Queensland and New South Wales are locked together in third place on 22 points.
In Adelaide, last-placed South Australia led by 378 runs after reducing Victoria to 46 for two at stumps on the third day.

Darren Lehmann, coming in at number three, had earlier steered South Australia into a strong position with an innings of 167 before captain Jamie Siddons declared on 449 for nine, an overall lead of 424.
